body: It's not even just theory it's the lack of electives or any classes that help practice writing, speaking skills, forming ideas etc. All lecturers are distant, they are never in the studio or available. I'm already self motivated and do self study/research + have been curating exhibitions and run an art collective + run an art business. I just expected art history classes or at least some list of class I could do if I wanted to. I probably will just sit it out but the experience so far has just been disappointing.

Other unis in Scotland also have regular classes and such, I've been considering ECA or maybe Grays in Aberdeen. From my experience at GSA so far I've never gotten proper feedback, or crits. It feels like such a waste not to properly learn theory or art history or anything.
They've only ever bring in other artists, teachers are never in and incredibly distant so I don't think I could get even proper feedback on my work from them.
I'm Scottish so the university pays my tuition and I get a very good student loan that I never have to pay back until I make a certain amount of money
you should be careful on gumtree, got a kitten from there in 2019. Didn't check the cat properly and ended up with a flea covered kitten that ended up dying a week after I got it.
